title: Risk quantification: likelihood, impact and expected value

videos.script: High, medium, low. Most risk lists stop there, and then a meeting argues about whether a medium is really a high. {{labels}} There is another way. Ask two questions with numbers for answers. How often will this happen in a year? And when it happens, what does it cost? {{two}} Multiply them, and you get the loss you should expect per year, in reais. Nine risks at the clinic come to a hundred and thirty-nine thousand a year, and one of them is more than half of it. {{sum}} The numbers are estimates, and you will learn to give them as ranges, because a range admits what you do not know. {{ranges}} And you will see two risks with exactly the same average that should not be treated the same way at all. {{same}}
